status: candidate differences reviewed in development; final acceptance pending

differences.source: Python store accepts caller now for retention cutoff and acknowledgement TTL scores; Valkey XADD still assigns real stream IDs. In-memory source also uses caller now and event occurred_at while publishing.
differences.native: Persisted retention, acknowledgement scores, expiry publication eligibility and physical TTLs use Valkey TIME, consistently with accepted W04. Event occurred_at preserves original finished_at or definition expiry; backlog age is clamped independently.
differences.reason: An arbitrary caller clock cannot delete durable events or change retention authority.

differences.source: Python validates canonical decimal cursors up to64 characters, but acknowledgement Lua compares tonumber components, rounding adjacent integers above2^53. Read forwards a valid oversize component to Valkey, which rejects IDs outsideu64.
differences.native: Same canonical decimal grammar and64-character bound, exact decimal length/lexical comparisons, exact future/expired distinction and read interval clamping for oversize sequences. Oversize millisecond values read empty and cannot be acknowledged past the tail.
differences.reason: Retain documented cursor precision and monotonic progression across source/native readers.

differences.source: Historical scripts do not preflight every mutable key type; a Lua command error may follow earlier changes.
differences.native: Retain accepted W04 raw-CAS/ownership/TTL/report-eviction preflight and add stream/ack/pause/expiry key-type checks before mutation; reject fully exhausted max-u64/max-u64 stream generation before writing. Valid old-timestamp/max-sequence streams still publish normally.
differences.reason: Lua does not roll back. A definite rejection must not publish partial report/baseline/outbox state. Trim/prune-only rejection side effects remain explicit source behavior.

differences.source: Legacy raw tenant:consumer acknowledgement suffix can collide when either accepted identifier contains colons; actual source-exact Lua/native characterization is retained.
differences.native: Length-delimited UTF8 tenant v2 acknowledgement key. Read-only structurally unambiguous legacy fallback; atomic monotonic migration on explicit ack. Ambiguous present legacy default read returns cursor_conflict before mutation; explicit replay returns acknowledgement_recovery and explicit retained ack establishes only the caller tenant/consumer v2 authority. Native authority wins; legacy bytes are never changed.
differences.reason: Preserve tenant/consumer fences without narrowing accepted identifier grammar or guessing historical ownership.
differences.migration: G04 drain-and-migrate required for legacy/native acknowledgement writers; no mixed-writer correctness or automatic ambiguous ownership claim.
